definitions.explanation: A feudal domain ruled by a daimyo during the Edo period (1603–1868). Japan was divided into roughly 300 han, each governed semi-autonomously under the Tokugawa shogunate.

examples.japanese: {薩摩|さつま}{藩|はん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{九州|きゅうしゅう}→九州：15647_kyuushuu⟧にあった。
examples.english: The Satsuma domain was in Kyushu.

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{藩|はん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{存在|そんざい}していた→存在する：17185_sonzaisuru⟧。
examples.english: Many feudal domains existed during the Edo period.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治|めいじ}{維新|いしん}→明治維新：16286_meijiishin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{藩|はん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦され→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{県|けん}→県：02151_ken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{置|お}かれた→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: The feudal domains were abolished and prefectures were established during the Meiji Restoration.

notes:
USAGE:
{藩|はん} is a historical term essential for understanding the Edo period. The system of {藩|はん} was formally abolished in 1871 through {廃藩置県|はいはんちけん} (abolition of domains and establishment of prefectures). Well-known domains include {薩摩|さつま}{藩|はん}, {長州|ちょうしゅう}{藩|はん}, and {土佐|とさ}{藩|はん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{藩主|はんしゅ}→藩主：26186_hanshu⟧: feudal lord (daimyo of a domain)
- {藩士|はんし}: domain samurai, retainer
- {廃藩置県|はいはんちけん}: abolition of domains and establishment of prefectures
- {藩校|はんこう}: domain school
- {雄藩|ゆうはん}: powerful domain
